transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Quiet, boy. Even the stones listen down here.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I fell in after my brother Omar. Did you see where the well took him?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I saw a boy dragged past the black fountain not long ago. What did he say to anger the well?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It was my fault. I dared him to insult it and the hand came for him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Then your tongue opened the door that swallowed him. Regret is heavy, but it will not pull him back.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I know that. Just tell me where he went so I can follow.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: There are paths that twist deeper where the glow grows thin. They do not stay the same for long.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then tell me the rules instead of the path. What do I need to survive here?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Fear feeds the well faster than blood. If you panic, you will forget why you came.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I will not forget Omar. I jumped down here for him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Many said the same when they first fell. The well thins memory like water through sand.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then give me something to hold on to. A charm, a sign, anything.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I have words that steady a heart. They are old and costly to remember.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then please give them to me. I cannot face whatever waits alone.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: No. Those words are not for every desperate soul who falls through the mouth of the well.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Why not? I came all this way for my brother.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Because courage borrowed from another man is thin courage. It snaps when the King of Jinn looks at you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then teach me how to grow it. I will listen.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Listen more than you speak. The dark counts every careless word.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Fine. I will be quiet if that helps me reach Omar.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Quietness is only the first step. Pride and anger must also stay buried.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: If I bring you something from above someday, would you help me then?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Gold means nothing here. The well has eaten kings richer than you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then I will help you escape when I get out. I promise.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Forty years have passed since I first heard that promise. The well does not return what it has swallowed.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: So you will just sit here forever?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Forever is only a word the surface uses to comfort itself. Down here we simply remain.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You could at least point me in the right direction.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Toward the deeper glow where the stone grows warm. That is where the well keeps the loud ones.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then that is where I will go.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Before you run, remember this: the King listens for trembling hearts.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: What does he want from people?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Silence and submission. Those who shout or beg amuse him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then I will not beg him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Good. Save your breath for the climb through fear.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Wait… what time is it anyway? It feels like night forever down here.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Time is a surface comfort that has no meaning in this pit. Speak of Omar instead of clocks.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Alright. Then tell me one last thing before I go.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: If you forget why you came, the well has already beaten you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I will not forget. Omar is the only reason I am still standing.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Then carry that memory carefully, boy. I will not help you further, so go and face the well alone.
